units.source: Attributes
In Trilium, attributes are key-value pairs assigned to notes, providing additional metadata or functionality. There are two primary types of attributes:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Labels__TRILIUM_PH_1__ can be used for a variety of purposes, such as storing metadata or configuring the behavior of notes. Labels are also searchable, enhancing note retrieval.
For more information, including predefined labels, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Labels__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Relations__TRILIUM_PH_1__ define connections between notes, similar to links. These can be used for metadata and scripting purposes.
For more information, including a list of predefined relations, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Relations__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
These attributes play a crucial role in organizing, categorizing, and enhancing the functionality of notes.
Types of attributes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Conceptually there are two types of attributes (applying to both labels and relations):

__TRILIUM_PH_0__System attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__As the name suggest, these attributes have a special meaning since they are interpreted by Trilium. For example the __TRILIUM_PH_3__ attribute will change the color of the note as displayed in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_5__ and links, and __TRILIUM_PH_6__ will change the icon of a note.

__TRILIUM_PH_0__User-defined attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1____TRILIUM_PH_2__These are free-form labels or relations that can be used by the user. They can be used purely for categorization purposes (especially if combined with __TRILIUM_PH_3__Search__TRILIUM_PH_4__), or they can be given meaning through the use of __TRILIUM_PH_5__Scripting__TRILIUM_PH_6__.

In practice, Trilium makes no direct distinction of whether an attribute is a system one or a user-defined one. A label or relation is considered a system attribute if it matches one of the built-in names (e.g. like the aforementioned __TRILIUM_PH_0__). Keep this in mind when creating  __TRILIUM_PH_1__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_2__ in order not to accidentally alter a system attribute (unless intended).

units.source: Multiplicity__TRILIUM_PH_0__

Attributes in Trilium can be "multi-valued", meaning multiple attributes with the same name can co-exist. This can be combined with __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to easily add them.
Attribute Inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_0__
Trilium supports attribute inheritance, allowing child notes to inherit attributes from their parents. For more information, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attribute Inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
